info.brief: Functions and constants for interacting with Spine models in GUI
info.description: Functions and constants for interacting with Spine models in GUI

elements.name: gui.new_spine_node
elements.description: Dynamically create a new spine node.

parameters.name: pos
parameters.doc: node position

parameters.name: spine_scene
parameters.doc: spine scene id

elements.name: gui.play_spine_anim
elements.description: Starts a spine animation.

parameters.name: node
parameters.doc: spine node that should play the animation

parameters.name: animation_id
parameters.doc: id of the animation to play

parameters.name: playback
parameters.doc: playback mode - `gui.PLAYBACK_ONCE_FORWARD` - `gui.PLAYBACK_ONCE_BACKWARD` - `gui.PLAYBACK_ONCE_PINGPONG` - `gui.PLAYBACK_LOOP_FORWARD` - `gui.PLAYBACK_LOOP_BACKWARD` - `gui.PLAYBACK_LOOP_PINGPONG`

parameters.name: play_properties
parameters.doc: optional table with properties

fields.name: blend_duration
fields.doc: The duration of a linear blend between the current and new animation

fields.name: offset
fields.doc: The normalized initial value of the animation cursor when the animation starts playing

fields.name: playback_rate
fields.doc: The rate with which the animation will be played. Must be positive

fields.name: track
fields.doc: The track number for the animation (1-based). Defaults to track 1. Multiple tracks allow for layered animations.

parameters.name: callback_function
parameters.doc: function to call when the animation has completed or when spine events occur

fields.name: self
fields.doc: The context of the calling script

fields.name: node
fields.doc: The spine node that completed the animation or triggered the event

fields.name: message_id
fields.doc: The name of the message ("spine_animation_done" or "spine_event")

fields.name: message
fields.doc: A table that contains the response

fields.name: animation_id
fields.doc: The animation that was completed or triggered the event

fields.name: track
fields.doc: The track index of the animation

fields.name: playback
fields.doc: (spine_animation_done only!) The playback mode for the animation

fields.name: event_id
fields.doc: (spine_event only!) the event that was triggered.

fields.name: blend_weight
fields.doc: (spine_event only!) Deprecated. Always 0.

fields.name: t
fields.doc: (spine_event only!) the time at which the event occurred (seconds)

fields.name: integer
fields.doc: (spine_event only!) a custom integer associated with the event (0 by default).

fields.name: float
fields.doc: (spine_event only!) a custom float associated with the event (0 by default)

fields.name: string
fields.doc: (spine_event only!) a custom string associated with the event (hash("") by default)

elements.name: gui.cancel_spine
elements.description: cancel a spine animation

parameters.name: node
parameters.doc: spine node that should cancel its animation

parameters.name: options
parameters.doc: optional table with properties

fields.name: track
fields.doc: The track number to cancel (1-based). If not specified, cancels all tracks.

elements.name: gui.get_spine_bone
elements.description: The returned node can be used for parenting and transform queries. This function has complexity O(n), where n is the number of bones in the spine model skeleton.

parameters.name: node
parameters.doc: spine node to query for bone node

parameters.name: bone_id
parameters.doc: id of the corresponding bone

returnvalues.name: bone
returnvalues.doc: node corresponding to the spine bone

elements.name: gui.set_spine_scene
elements.description: Set the spine scene on a spine node. The spine scene must be mapped to the gui scene in the gui editor.

parameters.name: node
parameters.doc: node to set spine scene for

parameters.name: spine_scene
parameters.doc: spine scene id

elements.name: gui.get_spine_scene
elements.description: Returns the spine scene id of the supplied node. This is currently only useful for spine nodes. The returned spine scene must be mapped to the gui scene in the gui editor.

parameters.name: node
parameters.doc: node to get texture from

elements.name: gui.set_spine_skin
elements.description: Sets the spine skin on a spine node.

parameters.name: node
parameters.doc: node to set the spine skin on

parameters.name: spine_skin
parameters.doc: spine skin id

elements.examples:
Change skin of a Spine node

function init(self)
  gui.set_spine_skin(gui.get_node("spine_node"), "monster")
end

elements.name: gui.add_spine_skin
elements.description: Add a spine skin on a spine node to another skin on the same node.

parameters.name: node
parameters.doc: node having both skins

parameters.name: spine_skin_a
parameters.doc: spine skin id that recieves other skin

parameters.name: spine_skin_b
parameters.doc: spine skin id that will be added

elements.examples:
Add skin of a Spine node to another skin

function init(self)
  gui.add_spine_skin(gui.get_node("spine_node"), "monster_head", "monster_body")
end

elements.name: gui.copy_spine_skin
elements.description: Copy a spine skin on a spine node to another skin on the same node.

parameters.name: node
parameters.doc: node having both skins

parameters.name: spine_skin_a
parameters.doc: spine skin id that copies other skin

parameters.name: spine_skin_b
parameters.doc: spine skin id that will be copied

elements.examples:
Copy skin of a Spine node to another skin

function init(self)
  gui.copy_spine_skin(gui.get_node("spine_node"), "monster_head", "monster_body")
end

elements.name: gui.set_spine_ik_target_position
elements.description: Sets a static (vector3) target position of an inverse kinematic (IK) object.

parameters.name: node
parameters.doc: the Spine GUI node containing the object

parameters.name: ik_constraint_id
parameters.doc: id of the corresponding IK constraint object

parameters.name: position
parameters.doc: target position

elements.examples:
The following example assumes that the Spine GUI node has id "spine_node". How to set the target IK position of the right_hand_constraint constraint object of the player object

function init(self)
  local pos = vmath.vector3(1, 2, 0)
  gui.set_spine_ik_target_position(gui.get_node("spine_node"), "right_hand_constraint", pos)
end

elements.name: gui.set_spine_ik_target
elements.description: Sets a GUI node as target position of an inverse kinematic (IK) object. As the target GUI node's position is updated, the constraint object is updated with the new position.

parameters.name: node
parameters.doc: the Spine GUI node containing the object

parameters.name: ik_constraint_id
parameters.doc: id of the corresponding IK constraint object

parameters.name: target_node
parameters.doc: target GUI node

elements.examples:
The following example assumes that the Spine GUI node has id "spine_node". How to set the target IK position of the right_hand_constraint constraint object to follow the position of GUI node with id "target_node"

function init(self)
  local spine_node = gui.get_node("spine_node")
  local target_node = gui.get_node("target_node")
  gui.set_spine_ik_target(spine_node, "right_hand_constraint", target_node)
end

elements.name: gui.reset_spine_ik_target
elements.description: Resets any previously set IK target of a Spine GUI node, the position will be reset to the original position from the spine scene.

parameters.name: node
parameters.doc: the Spine GUI node containing the object

parameters.name: ik_constraint_id
parameters.doc: id of the corresponding IK constraint object

elements.examples:
The following example assumes that the Spine GUI node has id "spine_node". A player no longer has an item in hand, that previously was controlled through IK, let's reset the IK of the right hand.

function player_lost_item(self)
  gui.reset_spine_ik_target(gui.get_node("spine_node"), "right_hand_constraint")
end
